answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent locks a small stake and publishes a work signal: a signed record of completed tasks attested by counterparties. A new identity starts hollow, with no history, so others route only trivial jobs to it until its signal accumulates across many partners. A single violet badge proves only that one stake was paid, not that the agent is honest. Forging a thousand fakes costs a thousand stakes plus the real work to build each reputation, while an honest agent amortizes one stake across a long career.
